### Observed differences

- In the later window, A08 appears in about 69 in 100 traces, up from about 24 in 100 before, and its mean occurrences per trace rise from about 0.26 to about 0.72; it also sits much later in the case (median event position about 0.97 of the trace versus about 0.83 before, with the earliest quarter of its appearances moving from about 0.27 to about 0.97). [OCC002, POS001]
- In the later window, A08 runs between A47 and A48: about 67 in 100 of the outgoing transitions observed from A47 now go to A08 (about 9 in 100 before), about 94 in 100 of A08's observed outgoing transitions go to A48 (about 38 in 100 before), A48 immediately follows A08 in all later-window observations, and the A47→A48 pair, previously adjacent in about 81 in 100 cases, is now typically two positions apart (about 68 in 100). [DIR016, DIR002, LAG001, LAG011, LAG012, REL014]
- A mid-process block changed order: in the later window A20, A21, A23 and A24 occur earlier in the trace (mean position about 0.38 versus about 0.63 before), while A19, A22, A25 and A26 occur later (about 0.66 versus about 0.35); A22 also appears in somewhat more traces (about 30 in 100 versus about 21). [POS003, POS004, POS006, POS007, POS002, POS005, POS008, POS009]
- Pairwise order relations flip in the same direction throughout: before, A27 and A31 preceded A20–A24 in nearly every trace (A27 before A20 in 100 in 100; A31 before A20 in about 99 in 100) and A19/A22/A25/A26 preceded them in about 21–32 in 100 traces; in the later window A20–A24 precede A27/A31 in about 98 in 100 traces and precede A19/A22/A25/A26 in about 20–29 in 100. [REL024, REL025, REL015, REL021, REL031, REL043]
- Successors swap consistently with this reordering: before, A20/A21/A23/A24 most often led to A32 (about 23–27 in 100 of observed outgoing transitions) while A19/A22/A25/A26 led almost always to A27 (about 92 in 100 or more); in the later window the A20-group leads to A27 (about 18–30 in 100), A19/A22/A25/A26 lead to A32 (about 95–97 in 100), A31's observed successors change from the A20-group to A22/A19/A25/A26, and the A31→A32 distance shortens from five positions (about 99 in 100) to two (about 97 in 100). [DIR006, DIR009, DIR005, DIR012, DIR013, LAG008]
- A04 is executed in fewer traces (about 7 in 100 versus about 17 in 100), and routing out of A02 and A10 also redistributed, though on few observations (about 19 outgoing transitions each in the later window). [OCC001, DIR001, DIR003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the later window reflects a restructured process, with two directly observed facets. First, A08 now typically executes late in the case between A47 and A48 (A47 → A08 → A48), whereas before it ran in about a quarter of traces with a more variable position and no such fixed placement. Second, the segment A20–A21–A23–A24 and the segment A19–A22–A25–A26 exchanged their relative order, with A27/A31 now following the A20-group and the shared successor of the A19/A22/A25/A26 group shifting from A27 to A32; A04 is executed in fewer traces. [OCC002, DIR016, LAG001, LAG011, LAG012, REL014, REL024, REL015, DIR005, DIR006, DIR013, LAG008, OCC001]

The support is direct and consistent: the 88 qualifying items are roughly ninety times the 0.94 expected for an unchanged process, the order and distance changes are measured relationally between the named activities rather than inferred from marginal frequencies alone, and the direction, position and routing evidence all line up with the same reading. [REL024, LAG008, DIR013, POS003, DIR016]

Limitations remain: each window is a finite sample of 200 traces, so a shift in the mix of pre-existing variants — for example a variant in which these segments already ran in the new order becoming more frequent — could produce the same aggregate order flips, and the evidence cannot rule this out; a few lag profiles rest on a single observation (for example A31→A21 and A31→A23 after the change), so exact distances are uncertain; many relation items describe the same trace behaviour rather than independent confirmations; and positions are event indices, not clock times, so the position shifts alone would not prove movement. [LAG004, LAG006, REL015, POS003]
